rust_authorities: The standalone Rust HTTP/SQLite runtime now directly coordinates matchmaking sessions and atomic signed-local/guest admission, the admitted fourteen-playlist catalog and eligibility/display projections, accepted-party commands/activity/consent/pregame countdown, and ticket create/poll/cancel with native rank SQL and gathering/QoS continuations. The same private queue source backs clans, parties, sessions and observed presence. No Python server or coordinator participates in these routes. An exclusive safe Owners queue transaction restores all native session, consent, countdown, continuation and RNG state when the actual SQLite COMMIT fails; SQL rolls back and provisional replies remain private. The canonical identity schema now owns legacy playlist_ranks DDL instead of the Python API. Actual failed-COMMIT controls cover ticket/rank publication, session replacement, signed-local allocation and countdown cancellation/retry. The original native countdown tick runs on a Rust timer; a real HTTP429 regression was fixed by using the existing separate countdown budget. Frozen native account, matchmaking and party clients use actual Rust HTTP: the current catalog admits zero playlists for v12 and twelve non-clan playlists for v16, and native Start/cancel observes the shared countdown. Provider handoff alone is a deterministic fixture. This modern runtime increment supplies no recovered original Live procedure, real provider grant, rendered UI or played-world proof. Search WebSocket IO, room/transport/EOS/voice/result integration, remaining social/provider issuance, complete clock/epoch/cross-process recovery, original service/config/order/arbitration recovery and full native/delivered G01-G12 acceptance remain open. The process keeps full readiness false and unported capabilities return503. No selected runtime or production service is activated.
